title: stabilize-intermittent-region-failover-and-variant-affinity-misbind
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Post-incident follow-up for an intermittently observed cross-region reroute oscillation that resulted in repeated fallback to incompatible model variants and elevated error/latency for customer traffic during peak hours. Ticket compiles timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations applied, and concrete engineering action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-27 03:12 UTC: First alert—region-eu reporting elevated 5xx and tail latency on generation routes. Autoscaler started adding capacity in eu-west-2.
2026-02-27 03:17 UTC: Smart-routing policy evaluated capacity metric; due to metric jitter, region fallback elected us-west-1 variant. Traffic started to reroute across regions.

2026-02-27 03:20 UTC: KV cache affinity mismatch detected—requests routed to us-west-1 attempted to use eu-optimized quantized variant. Latency and model errors increased; client errors (429/400) observed.
2026-02-27 03:23 UTC: Autoscaler in eu-west-2 reported scale-down followed by immediate scale-up (flapping) due to same noisy metric window, amplifying cross-region failover signals.
2026-02-27 03:29 UTC: Runbook manual mitigation: pinned routing decision to eu variant and applied temporary circuit-breaker to prevent further cross-region routing for affected route.
2026-02-27 04:10 UTC: Service stabilized after circuit-breaker and conservative autoscaler thresholds applied. Post-incident triage started.
2026-03-01: Postmortem readout completed; this ticket created to track engineering follow-ups.
root_cause: Multiple contributing factors: (1) routing decision logic used immediate short-window capacity signals without smoothing, causing oscillatory failover decisions when autoscaler jitter occurred; (2) fallback variant resolution lacked explicit compatibility checks for quantization/profile metadata, allowing mismatched variants to be selected across regions; (3) autoscaler hysteresis thresholds were too tight for bursty signal, producing scale-down/up flapping that amplified routing churn.
impact: Customer-facing increase in 5xx errors and tail latency for generation routes during the incident window (~17 minutes). Several mid-market customers reported degraded quality and increased costs due to repeated cold-model loads and cross-region egress. No data exfiltration or security compromise identified.
mitigation: Applied an emergency circuit-breaker to lock routing policy to local-region variants for the impacted route and temporarily relaxed autoscaler aggressiveness to add 60s stabilization window. We also reverted a recent routing policy change rolled out as canary earlier that week.
action_items: (A1) Implement smoothing on capacity signals used by smart-routing: add 3-window exponential decay and require sustained breach for 45s before failover. Owner: @Liam Chen. Due: 2026-03-15.

(A2) Add variant compatibility check to fallback resolver that validates model artifact metadata (quantization, tokenizer hash, config version) before selecting cross-region variant; fallback only to compatible variants. Owner: @Maya Rivera. Due: 2026-03-18.
(A3) Harden autoscaler hysteresis: introduce configurable min-stay and cooldown (default 120s) and expose in Dedicated config. Owner: @Priya Nair. Due: 2026-03-20.

(A4) Instrument routing decision path with delta telemetry: log pre/post-failover hash of variant metadata and capacity-window snapshot to enable causal tracing. Owner: @Andre Gomez. Due: 2026-03-12 (instrumentation shipped).

(A5) Create automated integration test that simulates noisy capacity signals and asserts routing stability and variant compatibility across regions. Owner: @Liam Chen and @Maya Rivera. Due: 2026-03-22.

(A6) Update runbooks: add explicit steps to disable cross-region routing per-route, how to pin variants, and checklist for circuit-breaker invocation. Owner: @Ops Runbook Team (Rachel Kim). Due: 2026-03-10 (drafted), 2026-03-17 (final).

(A7) Post-release verification: after runtime-1.20 changes, run a 72-hour synthetic soak with traffic patterns reproducing bursty load and confirm no oscillation. Owner: @Platform QA (Evan Park). Due: 2026-03-28.
(A8) Customer communication: inform impacted customers of root cause and mitigations; provide guidance for tenant-level pinning if needed. Owner: @Customer Success (Nora Malik). Due: 2026-03-16.

(A9) Maintain a short-term guardrail: add a soft quota that prevents more than two cross-region variant switches for a given request path within 10 minutes. Owner: @Liam Chen. Due: 2026-03-14 (deployed as precaution).
progress_updates: 2026-03-03: Emergency circuit-breaker implemented and deployed to production (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/842). Initial mitigation verified by SRE team.
2026-03-06: Instrumentation (A4) merged; routing traces now include variant metadata diffs (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/191).
2026-03-10: Runbook draft uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Region+Failover+Runbook. Feedback from Oncall reviewed.

2026-03-12: Smoothing change for capacity signals prototyped in staging; observed 3x reduction in failover churn under synthetic noise. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/856.
2026-03-14: Temporary soft quota (A9) deployed as precaution; monitoring dashboards added (Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/route-stability).
review_feedback: PM (Arjun Desai): prioritize variant-compatibility check before signal smoothing; argued it reduces blast radius faster.
SRE (Rachel Kim): recommended increasing autoscaler min-stay to 2 minutes as a baseline across clusters.
Security (Kai Zhou): confirmed no indication of security breach; requested logs retention extension for routing traces to 90 days for audits.
Design (Marin Alvarez): suggested adding a customer-facing dashboard widget showing regional affinity and last variant switch for transparency.
risks_and_open_questions: Risk: Compatibility check could reduce available fallback options during genuine region outages—need policy for forced cross-region fallback when no compatible variant exists.
Question: Should variant metadata schema be versioned to support graceful evolution of compatibility rules? Proposal: bump to v2 with explicit compatibility matrix. Input: @Maya Rivera.
Risk: Longer autoscaler hysteresis increases cost under short genuine spikes. Need cost/availability tradeoff decision for Dedicated customers.
closing_notes: This ticket will remain open until all A1-A9 items are closed and the post-release 72-hour soak shows no oscillation. Weekly touchpoint scheduled with cross-team owners on Thursdays at 09:00 UTC. Please add status updates to this ticket and link PRs or runbook changes as additional evidence.
